title: Addiction specialist (narcologist) visit
what: The doctor helps with dependence on alcohol, medicines and other substances. They also carry out exams for certificates.
why: For problems with alcohol or other substances, if you or your close ones are worried; for medical boards and certificates.
duration: the visit usually takes 20 to 40 minutes
tell_doctor: What, how often and how much you use - honestly, it will help your treatment
If you have had seizures or a severe state when you stopped
If you have liver or heart disease, or depression

prepare.title: Confidentiality
prepare.text: Ask the clinic in advance about anonymous visits, if that is important to you.

prepare.title: Before the visit
prepare.text: Come sober, so the doctor can assess your condition correctly.

prepare.title: Support
prepare.text: You can come with a close person.

bring: Hospital discharge summaries, if you have any
steps: The doctor calmly asks about your habits and health
Measures your blood pressure and pulse, examines you
May suggest a blood or urine test
Discusses with you what you want to achieve
Offers a plan of treatment and support
feel: Talking about dependence is hard - the doctor does not judge, but helps
after: Treatment is best started under a doctor's watch
With a strong dependence, stopping suddenly can be dangerous - discuss it with your doctor
Support groups help you keep the result
red_flags: Seizures, confusion or seeing things after stopping alcohol - call your local emergency number
Signs of poisoning: severe drowsiness, slow breathing - call your local emergency number

faq.q: Will my work find out that I saw an addiction specialist?
faq.a: Medical confidentiality is protected by law. Ask the clinic about anonymous visits.

faq.q: Can I quit on my own?
faq.a: Sometimes, but with strong dependence stopping suddenly is dangerous. It is better under a doctor's watch.

reminders.text: Addiction specialist visit tomorrow. Take your ID and list of medicines.
